target_customer: Hospital departments, residency (GME) programs and provider groups that outsource physician call, clinic and block scheduling
problem: Residents and attending physicians spend hundreds of hours a year on scheduling, and legacy tools display schedules rather than generate them.
business_model: Service plus software for outsourced physician scheduling, pricing not published

founders.name: Samuel Oberly
founders.background_notes: Mathematician per the YC page; degrees not specified.

founders.name: Zachary Dermody
education: Johns Hopkins, B.A. Economics, minor Computer Science, 2024

founders.name: Abdelrahman Hamimi
education: Johns Hopkins, M.S. and B.S. Computer Science, B.A. Economics, 2025
founders.background_notes: AWS Certified Cloud Solutions Architect per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Constraint-heavy schedule optimization with ACGME and department rules, plus an expanding workflow layer; hard on rules and trust, not on research.

defensibility.rationale: Hospital relationships and encoded department rules create stickiness, but QGenda, Amion and optimizer startups address the same job.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents display and publish schedules more than generate them per a rival vendor blog; no incumbent action against the company found.

market_need_then: Physician scheduling is manual and time consuming; the founders heard this directly from a Johns Hopkins doctor. Company reports 20 to 30+ departments across many hospitals (self-reported, counts vary by source).

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful promise: 'Never Schedule' and 'Making Your Scheduling Problems Disappear'

branding.brand_signature: Wizard metaphor with the tagline Never Schedule

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable and clear metaphor, but ShiftWizard by HealthStream is a confusable name in the same field. No press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Scheduling Wizard is an active YC Winter 2026 company with named academic medical customers and a services-first wedge in physician scheduling, expanding to triage and care coordination. No exit or layoffs reported, and funding beyond YC is not public, so traction is only self-reported so far.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked lists $500K pre-seed (March 2026) and Caplight lists $1M accelerator funding (2026-03-24) including a FastForward U grant; amounts conflict, no round recorded. Competition: no sources dated near 2024 found, only 2026 vendor comparisons naming QGenda, Amion, ShiftAdmin, Durate, Thrawn, so the list is left empty. HQ conflicts (Washington DC vs Wilmington). Round recorded rests on a single database (VCBacked); Caplight's $1M accelerator figure conflicts and is not recorded. A cross-check search found no press release or filing.
